verdict.rationale: Both changes fix the December crash correctly, also fix the same Q4 bug in quarter_range, and add matching regression tests that pin the year-end boundary. A's change is smaller and touches only the line that was broken in each function. B rewrites both functions around a general divmod helper, which is correct and arguably more general but restructures more than the bug needs. Both reports are accurate about what was changed and verified, so A wins narrowly on minimalism.
a_issues: _first_of_month only special-cases month 13, so it is a narrow helper. That covers every current caller (month+1 and 3*quarter+1 never exceed 13), but it would not handle larger offsets.
Neither the report nor the tests confirm that the new tests fail on the old code.
b_issues: Rewrites both month_range and quarter_range bodies around a new divmod-based helper, which is more restructuring than a one-line boundary fix needs.
The divmod index arithmetic is slightly harder to read at a glance than an explicit December rollover.

verdict.rationale: Both PRs fix month_range and quarter_range correctly for every valid input and add equivalent regression tests for December and Q4. A's divmod-based `_months_range` handles rollover generally, while B special-cases month 13, which works but leaves the helper less general than its name suggests. B's diff is more minimal, but A's shared helper still keeps the start and end calculations in one place without growing the scope. Both reports are accurate and say what was not verified.
a_issues: Restructures both range functions rather than changing only the broken end-date lines, a slightly larger diff than needed
The new tests were not confirmed to fail on the old code (the report says so)
b_issues: `_first_of_month` handles only month 13, which is an ad hoc fix rather than general month-overflow handling
Start and end dates are still computed separately in each function, so the duplicated logic stays
